title: The coat on the hook
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Thursday. The owner has put a hook by the backroom door. Not a word about it. Wood hangs the coat on it for the first time and cuts without it. The cut's no better. He puts the coat back on. The hook stays; it's hers now, for her coat.

panels.composition: A new brass hook on the backroom's doorframe. Fresh screw holes. The OWNER's doing. No note.

image.prompt: close on a new brass coat hook screwed into a doorframe with fresh screw holes, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD hanging the chore coat on it. Looking at the coat on the hook. Strange. The coat without him in it.

image.prompt: a young man hanging a canvas chore coat on a hook and looking at it as if at a stranger, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The cut. No better. The same.

image.prompt: close on a mat corner cut cleanly, no different from before, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The coat back on. The owner's coat on the hook instead, hers, at four. She says nothing. The hook's hers. Thirty strokes.

image.prompt: a young man back in his chore coat while a woman's coat hangs on the new hook, drawn in thirty sparse strokes, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: The hook. The coat off; no better. The hook's hers now.
